newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican earthquake damages houses, church.
newsitem.headline: Mexican earthquake damages houses, church.

text.p: An early morning earthquake on Thursday along Mexico's Pacific Coast damaged houses and a church in towns in the state of Michoacan, officials said.
Mexican media reports said the quake registered 5.9 on the Richter scale, but Colorado-based National Earthquake Information Service said the quake was 6.5 on the Richter.
Michoacan civil defence commander Alfonoso Lara said almost 60 percent of houses in the city of Arteaga, with 12,000 residents, suffered some sort of damage.
A church in the tourist town of Patzcuaro, a lake town well-known for its Day of the Dead ceremonies, was also reported damaged.
The quake hit at approximately 2:53 a.m. local time (0753 GMT) between the states of Guerrero and Michoacan, with the epicentre northwest of Petatlan, Guerrero.
The quake disturbed people sleeping throughout much of the central part of the country, but caused no injuries, officials said.
Many residents of Mexico City were roused from sleep during the quake, which lasted about a minute.
"There were no injured and minor damage to freeways in Michoacan state," Red Cross operations director Bernardino Heredia told Reuters.
Port officials at nearby Lazaro Cardenas and officials at resort cities of Ixtapa and Zihuatenejo could not be reached immediately for comment.
